newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BOLOGNA DENT SAMPDORIA'S TITLE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLOGNA DENT SAMPDORIA'S TITLE HOPES.

text.p: Russian Igor Kolyvanov scored twice, including a dramatic last-minute winner, as Bologna came from behind to win 2-1 at Sampdoria and deliver a serious blow to the Genoa club's Italian title hopes.
The result, Samp's second successive home defeat, gives Juventus a seven-point cushion at the top of Serie A after their 2-0 win over Vicenza in a match played on Saturday.

Sampdoria remain third on 36 points, two adrift of Inter, who won 3-0 at Piacenza in another Saturday fixture, and Parma, for whom Argentine Hernan Crespo scored twice in a 3-2 victory at home to relegation-threatened Cagliari.

Roma's Uruguayan striker Daniel Fonseca made an inspired appearance as a second-half substitute at the San Siro, equalising after 37-year-old Pietro Vierchowod's opener for Milan to earn his side a 1-1 draw against the lacklustre champions.

In a thrilling match between Atalanta and Perugia at Bergamo, Gianluigi Lentini salavaged a point for the home team with an 88th-minute goal to make it 2-2 after Perugia had overhauled them with goals in the 83rd and 86th minutes.
Russian Igor Simutenkov struck twice as bottom-of-the table Reggiana thrashed fellow strugglers Verona 4-2 for only their second win of the season.
